The proposed framework tackles the challenges of slow antenna movement, dynamic RCS variation, and imperfect CSI.
The proposed framework is a two-timescale optimization framework that jointly optimizes the discrete MA positions, communication and sensing beamforming vectors, and snapshot durations.
The goal of the optimization problem is to minimize the average transmit power at the base station while guaranteeing a minimum sensing and communication QoS.
The CSI acquisition process is performed at the beginning of the scanning period.
The resource allocation design process is performed at the beginning of the scanning period and involves jointly optimizing the beamforming vectors and snapshot durations.
The adjustment of MA process involves moving the antennas to the optimal positions at the beginning of the scanning period.
The communication and sensing process involves transmitting information symbols to the communication users and detecting potential sensing targets through reflected signals.
The signal model used in this paper is a complex Gaussian distribution.
The channel model used in this paper is a Rician channel model.
The distance matrix D is a matrix whose entry Dm,m1 represents the distance between the m-th and m1-th MA elements.
The minimum distance between any pair of MA elements is Dmin.

The goal of the proposed TTS framework is to minimize the average transmit power at the base station while guaranteeing a minimum sensing and communication QoS.
